# Egami.Svg: guide for coding agents

Egami.Svg reads, edits, saves and draws SVG 1.1 and SVG 2 (and SVGZ): an editable element tree, drawn through Egami.Drawing's
canvas onto rasters, PDF pages or SVG, with styles, text, filters and color fonts. It can also make `Raster.Load` read SVG files.

Namespaces: `Egami.Svg`, with `Egami`, `Egami.Pixels` and `Egami.Drawing`.

## Egami's vocabulary

Egami has its own names. Use them, not names from other imaging libraries: Egami has no `Image` type, no `Mutate` or `Clone`
and no `Configuration`.

- `Raster` and `Raster<TPixel>` hold an image; `TPixel` is a pixel type such as `Rgba8`, `Rgb8`, `Gray8`, `Bgra8` or `RgbaF32`
  (namespace `Egami.Pixels`). `Raster.Load` returns the type that fits the file; `Raster.Load<Rgba8>` converts while decoding.
- `Raster.Probe` reads a file's size, format and orientation without decoding it.
- `Apply(ops => ...)` changes a raster in place through a chain of operations; `Derive(ops => ...)` returns a new raster.
  `As<TPixel>()` converts to a new raster and `Copy()` duplicates one.
- `Save(path)` picks the writer from the extension; `Save(stream, format, options)` names it. Loading always detects the format
  from the bytes, never from the extension.
- `EgamiContext` holds the settings, `SafetyLimits`, thread count and registered formats a call uses. It is immutable: change
  it with `with`, and pass it to `Load` or `Probe`, or make it the default once at startup with `EgamiContext.SetDefault`.
- Every `Raster` owns pooled pixel memory: dispose it, best with `using`. `Derive`, `As` and `Load` return new rasters that you
  dispose too.

## Entry points

- `SvgDocument.Load(path)` and `SvgDocument.Parse(text)`, with `SvgLoadOptions` (resolver, DPI, strict mode, context).
- `document.Rasterize<TPixel>(new SvgRenderOptions { Width = ... })`: a raster; set a width or a height and the other keeps the
  aspect ratio.
- `document.Root`, `FindById`, `SvgElement.Attributes` and `Children`: the editable tree; `document.Save` writes it back.
- `EgamiContext.Default.WithFormat(SvgFormat.Info)`: SVG as an Egami format, so `Raster.Load` and `Raster.Probe` take .svg files.

## Samples

SVG to PNG:

```csharp
// An SVG drawn 256 pixels wide and saved as PNG; the height keeps the aspect ratio.
SvgDocument document = SvgDocument.Load(input);
using Raster<Rgba8> raster = document.Rasterize<Rgba8>(new SvgRenderOptions { Width = 256 });
raster.Save(output);
```

Load and read the warnings:

```csharp
// .svg and .svgz alike; nothing outside the file is opened unless a resolver allows it.
SvgDocument document = SvgDocument.Load(path);
Console.WriteLine($"{document.Title}: {document.Root.Descendants().Count()} elements");

// What a lenient load skipped is in Warnings, and in the context's diagnostics.
foreach (EgamiDiagnostic warning in document.Warnings)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{warning.Id}: {warning.Message}");
}
```

Edit the tree:

```csharp
SvgDocument document = SvgDocument.Parse(Icon);

// Elements, attributes and text are an editable tree, like XDocument's.
SvgElement body = document.FindById("body")!;
body.Attributes["fill"] = "#c33";
body.Attributes.Set("href", "#other", SvgNamespaces.XLink, "xlink");

SvgElement dot = new("circle");
dot.Attributes["cx"] = "12";
dot.Attributes["cy"] = "12";
dot.Attributes["r"] = "3";
document.Root.Children.Add(dot);
document.Root.Children.Add(new SvgComment(" added in code "));

foreach (SvgElement element in document.Root.Elements())
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{element.Name}: {element.Attributes.Count} attributes");
}
```

Let the file open what it refers to:

```csharp
// Images, style sheets and fonts the file refers to open only through a resolver; data: URIs always work.
var options = new SvgLoadOptions
{
    Resolver = SvgResolvers.SameDirectory(folder),
    Dpi = 96,
    Context = EgamiContext.Default with { Limits = SafetyLimits.Default with { MaxTotalBytes = 64L << 20 } },
};
SvgDocument document = SvgDocument.Parse(Icon, options);
```

`Raster.Load` for SVG files:

```csharp
// SVG as an Egami format: Raster.Load draws a file at its own size, Raster.Probe reads the size without drawing.
EgamiContext context = EgamiContext.Default.WithFormat(SvgFormat.Info);
RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe(path, context);
using Raster<Rgba8> icon = Raster.Load<Rgba8>(path, context);

// Twice the size, for a high-density screen.
using Raster<Rgba8> sharp = Raster.Load<Rgba8>(path, context, new SvgDecodeOptions { Scale = 2 });
```

## Common mistakes

- Expecting external images, style sheets and fonts to load. Nothing outside the file is opened unless
  `SvgLoadOptions.Resolver` allows it (`SvgResolvers.SameDirectory(folder)` for example); `data:` URIs always work. Keep it that
  way for files from users.
- Calling `Raster.Load` on an .svg without registering `SvgFormat.Info` in the context: core Egami does not read SVG.
- Expecting bad markup to throw. Loading is lenient and reports what it skipped in `document.Warnings`; set
  `Strict = true` to get an `SvgException` with the line and column.
- Text in fonts the machine lacks falls back to other fonts: give it the fonts the SVG names with `SvgLoadOptions.Fonts = new SvgFontOptions { Collection = fonts }`.
